title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Pain in the back and right side.

HPI: Patient is a 59-year-old male who presented for initial evaluation of a mass identified on imaging. He was diagnosed with cancer of the right lung. He has been undergoing chemotherapy for the primary malignancy. He reports mild shortness of breath and a persistent cough. He has been compliant with his current treatment regimen but notes increasing discomfort in his posterior thoracic region.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 98.6 F, Weight 195 lbs.

Recent Labs: WBC 7.2, Hgb 11.4, Plt 155, Creatinine 1.1, eGFR 82.

Medication List:
- Cisplatin (intermittent)
- Prednisone
- Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
- Ondansetron as needed for nausea

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fatigue and weight loss. Negative for fever or chills.
Respiratory: Positive for cough. Negative for wheezing or stridor.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for back pain and right-sided rib pain.
Neurological: Negative for numbness or tingling.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea or diarrhea.

Social History: Retired construction worker. Lives with wife. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Father had hypertension; Mother had diabetes.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in mild distress due to pain.
Respiratory: Decreased breath sounds noted in the right lung. No acute respiratory distress.
Musculoskeletal: Palpable tenderness over the thoracic spine and right posterior ribs. No obvious deformity.

Assessment:
1. Cancer of the right lung, currently receiving chemotherapy.
2. Bone metastases, presenting with localized pain.

Plan:
1. Continue current chemotherapy cycle as scheduled.
2. Initiate scheduled radiation therapy to address bone metastasis and alleviate pain.
3. Increase Acetaminophen dosage for breakthrough pain.
4. Follow up in 4 weeks for reassessment of pain levels and tolerance of treatment.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the right lung under current treatment is a current malignancy: C34.91.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
The note documents the right lung: use the right-lung code.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
